title: The native regular coefficient unit on a separably closed point is nonzero
statement: Let ℓ be prime and Ω a separably closed field. Let B be the condensed coefficient ring of finite-intermediate-field-valued continuous functions with values in Qbar_ℓ [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], and let B_SpecΩ be its pullback to the pro-etale site [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The tensor unit, equivalently the regular B_SpecΩ-module, in the category of internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is not a zero object. No restriction on the characteristic of Ω is needed.

source.place: isEquivalence_upperStarFromPointMod; use the monoidal unit comparison from WeilObject/Sheaf/StalkUnit.lean and evaluate the actual coefficient ring at a singleton.

proof.text: The condensed regular module is nonzero: if its identity were zero, forget to abelian sheaves, evaluate at a singleton profinite set, and apply the resulting equality to the constant section one. One would equal zero in the lifted subring of finite-intermediate-field-valued continuous functions, which is nontrivial. This follows directly from the definitions of padicAlgClRingObj and its ring presheaf.

Pullback from condensed modules to modules on Spec Ω is an equivalence for Ω separably closed. Its monoidal unit isomorphism identifies the native regular module with the pullback of the condensed regular module. If the native unit were zero, the image of the condensed unit would be zero. Full faithfulness reflects zero objects by IsZero.of_full_of_faithful_of_isZero, contradicting the first step.

theorem not_isZero_unit_on_separablyClosed_point
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] :
    ¬ IsZero (𝟙_ (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology (Spec (.of Ω))) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) (Spec (.of Ω)))))
